title: Tracehook proxy and metrics stitcher for per-service latency decomposition and burn-risk inspection
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Goal: Provide per-service and per-model visibility into tail latency and error contributions by stitching traces, metrics and logs at the request-span level. Deliver a lightweight Tracehook proxy + metrics-stitcher pipeline that: 1) enriches spans with model/route/token_count metadata, 2) writes high-cardinality tags to a dedicated metrics stream, and 3) emits stitchable event links into the log pipeline for SLO decomposition and burn-rate analysis.

Why this work: Current SLO alerts and burn-rate signals are coarse (service-level histograms). When latency spikes we lack a fast way to answer: is this caused by a particular model, route, client tier, or upstream dependency? That slows mitigation and increases noise. This ticket implements the edge of visibility (tracehook proxy) and the merge layer (metrics-stitcher) so runbooks and burn-rate alerts can be made model-aware.

Design notes / decisions:
- Component: tracehook-proxy (sidecar/proxy) sits in front of runtime pods and injects span tags and a short-lived flow-id. It will not store keys; it forwards enrichments as additional span attributes and emits a lightweight event to the stitcher topic.
- Stitcher: a stateless consumer that joins span attributes + metrics (histogram bucket emissions, RT metrics) by flow-id/span-id and emits aggregated records to the observability warehouse. It also computes per-request token counts and latency decomposition (decode vs attention vs IO).
- Sampling: adaptive sampling that increases capture to 100% for requests that push burn-risk thresholds (configurable by route/model). Baseline sampling default 1% per route.
- Rollout: canary to internal staging -> 5% production -> 25% -> 100%. Canary gated by CPU overhead (<5% p95), P50/P95 latency drift (<3%) and no increase in error rate.
- Alerts: create model-aware burn-rate alert rules that reference stitched metrics. Policy: fire page on sustained 4x burn above baseline for 15m or anomaly score >0.8 + 2x burn. Otherwise log-only.
- Dashboards: new Latency Decomposition dashboard (Grafana) with top contributing spans per model+route, token_count heatmap, and a small MTTI (mean time to identify) panel showing how long it takes to attribute a spike to a model.
- Security & privacy: tracehook only surfaces model name, route, and anonymized customer tier; no raw prompt or PII forwarded. Must go through security review before full prod.

Non-goals: replacing full distributed tracing stack, storing payloads, or building heavy correlation backfills. This is a low-latency augmentation to existing traces and metrics.

Performance targets (acceptance metrics):
- CPU overhead of tracehook-proxy: p95 <= 5% on runtime pod CPU during normal traffic.
- Latency drift: additional added latency at p50/p95 <= 3% absolute (should not push SLO).
- Stitch latency: stitched aggregate record available in ingestion warehouse within 90s.
- False attribution rate: <10% (manual validation with labeled set).

Acceptance criteria:
- Tracehook proxy built, unit tested, and running in staging.
- Metrics-stitcher service processes staging topic and writes aggregated records to the warehouse schema (stitch_v1).
- Grafana dashboard created and surfaced on console under Observability -> Latency Decomp.
- Burn-rate alert rules implemented in staging and exercised via synthetic load with expected alert behaviors.
- Canary plan documented and approved by SRE and Security.

Implementation plan / milestones:
1) 2026-02-20 -> 2026-02-28: Design review, schema, and proto for flow-id and stitch record.
2) 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-07: Implement tracehook-proxy sidecar shim + integration test harness.
3) 2026-03-08 -> 2026-03-12: Metrics-stitcher consumer, aggregation logic and local end-to-end tests.
4) 2026-03-13 -> 2026-03-18: Deploy to staging, create dashboards, run synthetic attribution tests.
5) 2026-03-19 -> 2026-03-28: Canary rollout and post-canary signoff.

Runbook / Oncall behavior (high level):
- Pager severity mapping: Critical page if burn-rate >=4x and sustained >15m affecting >25% customers; otherwise page on anomaly score >0.9 for customer-facing tier.
- Triage steps: check Latency Decomp dashboard -> identify top model/route -> check recent deploys (gitlab commit lookup) -> if model-specific, throttle traffic or fallback to smaller model variant.
- TODO: add automatic fallback policy to routing layer once feature flag is ready.
